title: The Society of Agents
subtitle: When the Org Chart Starts Thinking

slots.anchor: Sixteen Claudes were building a compiler.
slots.brief: Corner scene: a long workshop hall, sixteen small hand-built robots at individual desks — each doing something visibly different (one reads, one solders, one files papers, one argues with a test bench); on the wall a branching tree of string and pinned cards (git history, unlabeled). Not a crowd of identical robots — a society shown through different positions and activities.

slots.anchor: Some of the earliest surviving writing
slots.brief: Margin vignette: a Mesopotamian clay tablet with cuneiform grain accounts; resting beside it, a robot's small paper note pinned with the same care — two external memories five thousand years apart, drawn as siblings. No readable modern text.

slots.anchor: ## A Man in a Dark Room
slots.brief: Margin vignette: a darkened room, one small aperture, a single ray of light crossing to a wall; a robed figure (Ibn al-Haytham, seen from behind) arranging a mirror in the beam. The apparatus is the argument.

Corner scene: Boyle's brass air-pump mid-demonstration, three periwigged witnesses leaning in with different expressions (awe, doubt, note-taking); a small robot assistant holds the leaky joint with one finger, looking at the reader. Reality pushed back against the package.

slots.caption: A society organized around an argument with reality
slots.brief: Framed plate: the vast interior of a particle detector rendered as watercolor cathedral — tiny human figures on gantries, layered instrument rings like rose windows. Awe without sci-fi glow; the machine as an institution made physical.
